text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=redwood-inference-autoscaler queue_depth > 1200 for 2m, urgency=high, pd_incident=PD-84213
maya: acked in PD, i'm on it — looking at autoscaler metrics now :eyes:
pd-bot: PD-84213 acknowledged by maya
maya: quick snapshot: avg queue size 1250, tail latency 2.8s, dropped requests ~4% over last 3m. autoscaler desired=12, current=12, avg cpu 36% but queue growing. looks like scaling algorithm not kicking in on queue metric.
nana?: (sorry wrong channel)
simon: @maya thanks — can you share the autoscaler controller logs and the scale decision history?
maya: pulling logs, past 10m from scale-controller:```
2026-03-14T14:01:02Z INFO evaluate_scale: observed_queue=320, desired=10
2026-03-14T14:02:02Z INFO evaluate_scale: observed_queue=450, desired=10
2026-03-14T14:03:02Z INFO evaluate_scale: observed_queue=780, desired=10
2026-03-14T14:04:02Z INFO evaluate_scale: observed_queue=1120, desired=12
2026-03-14T14:05:02Z WARN scale-delay: cool_down active, last_scale=49s, skip_scale
2026-03-14T14:06:02Z INFO evaluate_scale: observed_queue=1250, desired=12
2026-03-14T14:06:03Z ERROR reconciliation: failed to create pod: Insufficient capacity in pool "g4dn-pool-2"
```
maya: summary: controller wanted to scale but cloud provider returned Insufficient capacity. fallback policy didn't pick other pools.
katie-oncall: customer-facing note: prelim impact: POST generation requests returning 503s and some timeouts. I saw spikes in Sentry for model-inference timeouts.
simon: ok, plan: (1) try burst to alternative pool (2) increase preemptible fallback (3) open provider capacity request if needed. Any quick mitigation to reduce customer pain?
maya: i can flip autoscaler policy to allow cross-pool bursting now. command:```bash
# allow-burst to fallback pool
ctl autoscaler update-policy --name inference-autoscaler --allow-pool-burst=true --burst-pools g4dn-pool-3,g5-spot-pool
```
maya: executing...
ops: (deploy-bot) ran ctl autoscaler update-policy — status=ok
maya: triggering manual scale for immediate relief:```bash
ctl scale deployment inference-workers --replicas=18 --reason "emergency burst due to PD-84213"
```
maya: kubectl output:```
Scaled deployment "inference-workers" to 18 replicas
Events: 6 FailedScheduling: 4/6 pods failed to schedule due to insufficient zone capacity
```
liam: @maya if scheduling is failing in zone A, can we spread across zone B/C? do we have node pools in those zones?
maya: there are g5 spot pools in zone-b and g4dn reserved in zone-c; the autoscaler policy was restrictive on instance family. i'm widening now.```bash
ctl autoscaler update-policy --name inference-autoscaler --allowed-families g4dn,g5 --allow-cross-zone=true
```
maya: update applied. kube events now showing some pods scheduled in zone-b.
nana again: (ignore)
simon: how's the queue look after the manual scale?
maya: queue depth dropped from 1250 -> 420 in ~90s. tail latency down to 1.1s. error rate falling to 0.8% (was 4%). progress. :thumbsup:
katie-oncall: note for incident timeline: 14:01 alert triggered, 14:05 autoscaler hit capacity, 14:08 pd ack, 14:09 manual policy change to allow bursting, 14:11 manual scale request, 14:13 queue reduced to ~420, 14:14 errors trending down.
nana: are there any customer escalations?
katie-oncall: support queue has two Priority-1 tickets opened by customer X and customer Y reporting generation failures. I've posted a short status update to the customers and product.
simon: next steps: (A) keep bursting/config until provider replenishes capacity (B) create temporary routing to lower-cost model variant to reduce load (C) postmortem to root cause why fallback pools weren't used automatically.
maya: i can add a routing rule to steer lower latency, lower-cost model for non-SLA traffic:```yaml
routing:
  default: large-model-v2
  emergency-overflow: small-quantized-v1 (weight 0.6 for non-critical paths)
```
maya: applied rule in dev, rolling to prod now.
pd-bot: PD-84213 status changed: triggered -> acknowledged -> resolved? (manual close pending)
liam: handing off to @liam for the rest of the shift — I'll stay reachable for 15m if anything regresses. Handoff notes: current queue 410, replicas 16 running, pending pods 2, provider capacity request id=CR-7791 created.
simon: @liam pls keep an eye on drop rate and scheduler events. escalate to infra if Insufficient capacity persists.
liam: acked PD and taking over. I'll check provider portal and the capacity request ETA.
katie-oncall: k, i'll update customers with ETA=~30m for capacity fix, and link to status page. anyone want me to include a workaround note re: temporary lower-quality model?
maya: yes please include the workaround and apology, mention we rolled a temporary routing and manual scaling.
simon: i've filed initial incident and set Sev=2, assign to eng-runtime for postmortem. tags: autoscaler, capacity-exhaustion, provider-failover, customer-impact.
liam: quick check 15m after handoff: queue 220, error rate 0.3%, tail latency 0.9s. will monitor.
katie-oncall: thanks all. closing PD if stable in 30m. :white_check_mark:
